reasoning.title: Expand and paginate reviews
reasoning.description: Use when a product’s reviews are hidden in a collapsed tab or extend across multiple pages; not when all reviews are already visible on one page.
reasoning.content: Open the tab labeled “Reviews,” inspect every displayed review, then follow the review section’s visible pagination controls until no unvisited page remains. Do not mistake returning to a previous page for proof that all pages were inspected.

reasoning.title: Ground every reviewer match
reasoning.description: Use when listing reviewers whose text mentions a requested product characteristic; not when the task only asks for an aggregate review count.
reasoning.content: For each match, visibly verify the reviewer name and the qualifying review sentence together on the page before recording it. Keep a page-by-page evidence list and report only names supported by observed text, including close semantic matches only when the wording clearly expresses the requested characteristic.

reasoning.title: Expand and traverse Reviews
reasoning.description: Use when review content is hidden behind a product-page tab and the request requires checking the complete review set; not when reviews are already fully visible.
reasoning.content: Select the tab labeled “Reviews” and inspect every displayed review. Continue through any visible pagination or “Next” control until no unvisited review page remains; the count in the tab is only a total, not proof that all entries are loaded.

reasoning.title: Verify matches and return reviewer names
reasoning.description: Use when identifying reviewers whose review text mentions a concept, including wording variations; not when the task asks only for aggregate ratings.
reasoning.content: Read each review body and check reasonable spacing, inflection, and synonymous phrasing rather than relying on one exact string. Record the reviewer name attached to each verified match, then always provide a final answer, explicitly stating when no matching reviewers were found.

reasoning.title: Expand the Reviews tab and ground each match
reasoning.description: Use when the product page shows reviews inside a collapsed tab; not when reviews are already visibly expanded.
reasoning.content: Click the tab labeled “Reviews” before evaluating matches. For every qualifying review, keep both the visible reviewer name and the exact review-text phrase in the trace so the result is verifiable.

reasoning.title: Traverse review pagination explicitly
reasoning.description: Use when the expanded Reviews section has page links or a “Next” control; not when all reviews appear on a single page.
reasoning.content: Inspect the visible reviews on the current page, then click the review section’s next-page control and repeat until it is disabled or absent. Record each page transition and do not claim exhaustive coverage from the review count alone.

reasoning.title: Expand the Reviews tab
reasoning.description: When review text is hidden on a product page; not needed if reviewer names and full review bodies are already visible.
reasoning.content: Select the tab labeled “Reviews” and verify that the review section expands. Read every displayed review body rather than relying on the tab’s review count or summary.

reasoning.title: Map matching text to reviewer names
reasoning.description: When asked which reviewers express a particular opinion; not for tasks requesting only ratings or aggregate review totals.
reasoning.content: Check each review for direct wording or clear equivalents of the requested sentiment, then record the reviewer name attached to each match. After inspecting all reviews, always return the matching names or explicitly state that none qualify.

reasoning.title: Verify the complete reviewer identity
reasoning.description: Use when returning reviewer names based on matching review language; not when the task requests only aggregate ratings or counts.
reasoning.content: Before reporting a match, ensure one page observation visibly contains both the qualifying review sentence and the reviewer’s complete displayed name. Never infer or autocomplete a surname from truncated text; expand the review, inspect its author label, or navigate to a view where the full name is exposed.

reasoning.title: Traverse every review page
reasoning.description: Use when the Reviews section includes pagination or indicates more reviews than are currently displayed; not when the full set is shown on one page.
reasoning.content: Inspect every visible review on the current page, then use the pagination control such as “Next” or a page link and repeat until no unvisited page remains. Record each qualifying reviewer and quotation only from visibly observed review text, rather than relying on narration or the displayed review count.

reasoning.title: Expand the Reviews section before extracting
reasoning.description: Use when review content is collapsed behind the product-page tab labeled “Reviews”; do not rely on the tab’s count or narration as evidence of review text.
reasoning.content: Click the visible “Reviews” tab and verify that each candidate’s reviewer name and review text are rendered on the page. Record a reviewer only when the visible text explicitly discusses the requested issue or a clear synonym.

reasoning.title: Verify every review page through visible pagination
reasoning.description: Use when the expanded review section shows pagination; not needed when all reviews are visibly present in a single list.
reasoning.content: After inspecting the current review list, use the visible page-number or “Next” control beneath it and confirm that the displayed reviews change. Continue until no unvisited page remains, keeping visible name-and-text evidence from each page before answering.

reasoning.title: Open the full order history
reasoning.description: Use when the account dashboard shows only recent orders; not needed if already on the “My Orders” page.
reasoning.content: From “My Account,” open “My Orders” rather than relying on the dashboard’s recent-order summary. Use the per-page selector to choose the largest available page size, and confirm whether pagination remains before treating the list as exhaustive.

reasoning.title: Verify visible order-row fields
reasoning.description: Use before reporting a date-filtered count or spending total from order history.
reasoning.content: Read the visible date, status, and order-total fields for every qualifying row, paging as needed. Do not infer results from the total order count or page setting; only count rows whose displayed status matches the requested state and sum their displayed totals.

reasoning.title: Open the complete order history
reasoning.description: Use when a task requires checking orders beyond the account summary; not needed when the requested order is already fully shown in Recent Orders.
reasoning.content: From “My Account,” open “My Orders.” Use the page-size selector labeled with an items-per-page option and choose the largest available size; if the history still spans multiple pages, inspect every page.

reasoning.title: Verify order rows before aggregating
reasoning.description: Applies to any count or spending total filtered by date and order status; do not rely on the displayed total number of orders or pagination settings alone.
reasoning.content: After the page refreshes, confirm that the order table visibly exposes each relevant row’s date, status, and amount. Filter rows by the requested period and exact status, then count those rows and sum their displayed totals; if rows are not visible in the observation, scroll or inspect the page rather than inferring a zero result.

reasoning.title: Verify visible order-row evidence
reasoning.description: Use before reporting any date-filtered count or spending total, especially after changing the page size or navigating between history pages.
reasoning.content: Confirm that the “My Orders” page visibly exposes each relevant row’s order date, status, and amount before calculating. If the observation contains only the header or navigation, wait, scroll, refresh, or re-observe until the rows are present; never infer results from the page count or claim that rows loaded without row-level evidence.

reasoning.title: Open and expand full order history
reasoning.description: Use when a task requires analysis beyond the recent-order summary shown on the account dashboard; not needed when the requested order is already fully visible there.
reasoning.content: From “My Account,” open “My Orders,” then use the page-size selector to choose the largest available option. Confirm that all orders are shown by checking the displayed-results text and pagination; if pages remain, inspect each page.

reasoning.title: Verify every qualifying order row
reasoning.description: Use when counting or totaling orders by date, fulfillment status, or amount; not for merely locating the order-history page.
reasoning.content: Read the visible order table and record each qualifying row’s order date, status, and grand total before calculating. Apply the date boundary and exact displayed status consistently, and never derive a result solely from the total order count or the claim that all rows are loaded.

reasoning.title: Ground aggregates in visible order rows
reasoning.description: Use whenever counting orders by date or status or summing order totals; do not calculate if the trace only exposes page chrome and no order table rows.
reasoning.content: Inspect and record each qualifying row’s visible order date, status, and total, scrolling or paging until every relevant row has been observed. Reconcile the recorded row count with the history’s displayed-range or pagination indicator, then sum only rows whose visible status and date satisfy the task.

reasoning.title: Open complete order history
reasoning.description: Use when a task requires reviewing all purchases rather than only recent activity; the account dashboard is insufficient.
reasoning.content: From “My Account,” open the “My Orders” link to reach the full order-history page. Use the page-size selector to choose the largest available option, but treat this only as a display setting—not proof that every order loaded.

reasoning.title: Verify rows before aggregating
reasoning.description: Use whenever counting or totaling orders by date, status, or amount; do not proceed if the observation shows only the page header or navigation.
reasoning.content: After changing the page size, wait for the page to reload and confirm that order rows visibly include the order date, status, and amount, and that no additional pagination remains. Calculate only from those observed rows, filtering by the requested date range and the visible fulfillment label; if rows are absent or truncated, re-observe or traverse every page instead of inferring totals from a header count.

reasoning.title: Build totals from visible row fields
reasoning.description: Use when counting orders by fulfillment state or summing spending over a date range.
reasoning.content: For each qualifying row, record the displayed order date, status, and order total, treating “Complete” as the site’s fulfilled status unless the task defines fulfillment differently. Keep a visible row-by-row tally and sum only qualifying totals so the reported count and amount can be verified from the trace.

reasoning.title: Open the complete order table
reasoning.description: Use when the account dashboard shows only a Recent Orders preview; not when the requested records are already fully visible.
reasoning.content: From “My Account,” follow the “My Orders” or full-history link beside “Recent Orders.” On “My Orders,” use the page-size selector to choose its largest option, then confirm the order count fits on the displayed page; otherwise inspect every pagination page.

reasoning.title: Ground totals in visible rows
reasoning.description: Use whenever counting or summing orders by date and fulfillment status.
reasoning.content: For each qualifying row in the “My Orders” table, capture the displayed order date, status, and order total. Apply the date boundaries consistently, include only rows whose visible status denotes fulfillment, and keep a row-by-row tally and running sum before reporting the result.

reasoning.title: Use the full My Orders history
reasoning.description: When identifying the latest order, rather than reviewing a specific known order or only the account dashboard.
reasoning.content: From “My Account,” open the “My Orders” link and inspect the visible order-history rows. Confirm the displayed sort order or compare the visible order dates before opening the newest row’s “View Order” link; do not assume the first row is newest without page evidence.

reasoning.title: Verify status and arrival details from visible labels
reasoning.description: When reporting an order’s status, order date, or expected arrival from an order-history row or order-detail page.
reasoning.content: On the order page, capture the text shown beside the date and status labels and look for a shipment, tracking, or expected-delivery section. The page title and URL establish only which order is open; if no arrival estimate is displayed, report that it is not shown rather than inferring one from the narrated status.

reasoning.title: Expose and verify the oldest order
reasoning.description: Use when the “My Orders” page paginates results or defaults to showing only a subset; pagination may be skipped only when every order is already visible.
reasoning.content: Use the page-size selector below the order list and choose its largest available option, then follow any remaining pagination to the final page. Read the visible “Order Date” cells and report the oldest date only after confirming the relevant row is displayed; do not rely solely on the total-order count or assumed sort direction.

reasoning.title: Verify the order table before answering
reasoning.description: Use when reporting a purchase date or identifying the earliest/latest order from “My Orders.”
reasoning.content: After changing the page size, confirm that the visible order table includes its date column and all expected rows. Determine the sort direction and read the boundary row directly; if the table or date is absent from the observation, scroll or re-observe rather than inferring the answer.

reasoning.title: Use autocomplete to refine product searches
reasoning.description: When a broad query triggers a visibly relevant suggestion beneath the store search box; not when no suggestion matches the user’s need.
reasoning.content: Select the matching autocomplete suggestion, then open a result whose visible title explicitly addresses the requested condition or use case. Do not infer suitability from nearby or similarly named results.

reasoning.title: Verify product-page claims after expanding Reviews
reasoning.description: When reporting price, availability, ratings, reviewer identity, or review text from a product page; not when making only a recommendation based on the visible product title.
reasoning.content: Confirm price and stock in the visible purchase area, then activate the labeled “Reviews” section and read the rendered rating and review entries. Omit any detail that does not become visibly available after expansion; a successful click alone is not evidence that review content loaded.

reasoning.title: Use price sorting in both directions
reasoning.description: When a search asks for the full price range across matching products; not when it asks about a single product or a filtered subset.
reasoning.content: On the search-results page, choose “Price” from the sort control, then use the adjacent sort-direction toggle to inspect both ascending and descending order. Read the first product’s displayed price in each direction as the candidate minimum and maximum.

reasoning.title: Capture literal price evidence
reasoning.description: Whenever reporting extrema from sorted results, especially after a sort or direction change; not if both endpoint prices are already visibly present in the page observation.
reasoning.content: After each sort, wait for the results to refresh and inspect the product grid until the first item’s price is literally visible in the observation. Do not infer an endpoint from the URL, result count, sort state, or prior narration; if the price is not shown, scroll or inspect the first product card before answering.

reasoning.title: Use price sort in both directions
reasoning.description: Apply when a task asks for the minimum, maximum, or full price range across search results; not when only one specific product’s price is needed.
reasoning.content: On the results page, choose “Price” in the sort control, then use the adjacent direction link. Its label describes the action it will perform—such as “Set Ascending Direction”—so verify the resulting direction and read the first product card, then toggle direction and read the new first card.

reasoning.title: Require visible endpoint evidence
reasoning.description: Apply whenever values must be extracted from sorted results, especially after a click timeout or when the page observation shows only the header; not when the relevant product card and price are already visible in the trace.
reasoning.content: After every sort or direction change, scroll to or inspect the product grid and capture the first item’s visible price before recording it. A changed URL or failed-click side effect may indicate navigation occurred, but it is not evidence of the endpoint until the sorted product card and price are visibly observed.

reasoning.title: Use fielded Advanced Search
reasoning.description: Apply when the main Search box returns broad, unrelated matches; do not use when ordinary results are already specific enough.
reasoning.content: Open the “Advanced Search” link and place brand or model terms in “Product Name,” with product-type terms in “Description,” then activate the “Search” button. If an exact phrase returns nothing, broaden the fields incrementally rather than reverting to an unrestricted site search.

reasoning.title: Verify prices in the rendered product list
reasoning.description: Apply before reporting any price range from search results, especially when the current observation shows only the page header; a result count or claimed inspection is not evidence of product prices.
reasoning.content: Scroll until product cards with names and prices are visibly present, inspect every results page, and record only items that match the requested category. Use the “Sort By” control with “Price” and confirm the direction control’s visible state, but report endpoints only after both corresponding products and prices appear in the trace.

reasoning.title: Use complete order history
reasoning.description: When reviewing purchases for a date range; do not rely on the account dashboard’s recent-orders summary.
reasoning.content: Open the “My Orders” link from “My Account,” then inspect every visible order row and any additional pages until dates pass the target range. Record the displayed date and “View Order” link for each matching row; the recent-orders table is only a partial look-alike.

reasoning.title: Verify item-level charges
reasoning.description: When totals depend on product category rather than entire order totals; not when the task asks for whole-order spending.
reasoning.content: Open each matching order with “View Order” and ground every included item in the visible product name, quantity, and item subtotal. Add only verified item-level charges, and explicitly handle shipping, tax, discounts, and ambiguous products instead of inferring them from the order total.

reasoning.title: Sum qualifying item subtotals
reasoning.description: Use when only certain product categories within an order count; do not use the whole order total merely because the order contains one qualifying item.
reasoning.content: On each order-detail page, verify the visible product names and add only the displayed subtotals for qualifying items. Exclude unrelated merchandise and shipping unless the task explicitly requests them, and keep the calculation grounded in values shown on the page.

reasoning.title: Expand and verify the full order history
reasoning.description: Use when the account dashboard shows only recent orders or the requested period may span older history; skip when all relevant orders are already visible.
reasoning.content: Open the visible “My Orders” link, use the page-size selector to show the maximum available rows, and read each visible order date before opening matching “View Order” links. Do not claim complete coverage unless the dates and pagination state are actually present in the observed page output.

reasoning.title: Capture item and total evidence from each order
reasoning.description: Use when calculating spending by product type from one or more orders; order-list summaries alone are insufficient.
reasoning.content: On every matching order page, scroll to and observe the “Items Ordered” table and totals section, recording each product name, price, quantity, line subtotal, and “Shipping & Handling” charge. Base the final calculation only on those visible fields, and explicitly state whether shipping is included rather than silently omitting or assigning it.

reasoning.title: Expand the full order history
reasoning.description: Use when the requested purchase date is older than the orders shown on the account dashboard; this is unnecessary when the target order is already visible.
reasoning.content: Open “My Orders” from the account area, then use the “Show” per-page selector to display enough orders to cover the requested date. Match the date in the history table before opening the order via its order link or “View Order” action.

reasoning.title: Verify item and total details on the order page
reasoning.description: Use when the task filters spending by category, product type, or date; an order-history total alone is sufficient only when the task asks for the entire order amount.
reasoning.content: On the “Order #” page, inspect the visible order date, “Items Ordered” table, product names, quantities, subtotals, and order totals before calculating. Do not report an amount unless those fields are present in the observation; scroll or retrieve more page content if the trace only shows the header/navigation.

reasoning.title: Load the complete order history
reasoning.description: Use when calculating spending over a past date range; do not rely on the account dashboard or the first history page.
reasoning.content: Open “My Account” → “My Orders,” then use the items-per-page selector’s largest option or page through every result until the full date range is covered. Returning from an order detail page may reset the list size, so reapply the selector or use the pagination controls before concluding that all relevant orders were found.

reasoning.title: Verify each order from visible details
reasoning.description: Use when spending depends on product type, category, or excluding nonqualifying merchandise; order dates alone are insufficient.
reasoning.content: Open each in-range order with its visible “View Order” link and verify the displayed date, line-item names, quantities, and prices or totals. Classify food only from visible product information and sum qualifying line items; if the result is zero, explicitly ground it in the inspected line items rather than unsupported narration.

reasoning.title: Verify each order’s itemization
reasoning.description: Use when spending must be filtered by product category, fulfillment status, or cost component; not needed when the task asks only for an unfiltered total already shown in the history table.
reasoning.content: Open each potentially relevant order through its visible order link and confirm the product names, status, item subtotal, shipping, and grand total in the order-details sections. Do not classify products or report amounts unless those labeled fields are visibly present; if page output is truncated, scroll or retrieve additional content before calculating.

reasoning.title: Verify qualifying items inside each order
reasoning.description: Use when spending must be limited by product type, category, or order status; not when the task asks for the total of an entire known order.
reasoning.content: Open each date-matching order with its visible “View Order” control, exclude canceled orders, and inspect the item names, categories, and charged amounts on the order-detail page. Report a sum only after those qualifying items and amounts are literally visible in the trace; if the page evidence is truncated, scroll or capture the relevant section before calculating.

reasoning.title: Verify configuration in the order details
reasoning.description: Use when the requested attribute belongs to an item in a specific past order; do not answer when only the order header or navigation area is visible.
reasoning.content: Open the matching order with its “View Order” link, then scroll or retrieve more page content until the “Items Ordered” section and the product’s labeled configuration are visibly present. Report only text directly observed there; a matching order date alone does not establish the item or its options.

reasoning.title: Reapply the order-history display limit
reasoning.description: Use when returning to “My Orders” after inspecting an order and the older target is no longer listed; it is unnecessary if the target row remains visible.
reasoning.content: The “Show” selector can reset to the default number of orders after navigating back. Select a larger visible page size again, then locate the intended row and use that row’s “View Order” link rather than clicking by remembered position.

reasoning.title: Expand the complete order history
reasoning.description: Use when the purchase is older than the orders shown on the account overview; not needed when it already appears in recent orders.
reasoning.content: Open “My Orders,” then use the “Show” selector to choose the largest page size so the full history is visible. Restrict candidates by the displayed purchase year rather than guessing from order total or item count.

reasoning.title: Inspect candidates systematically and read item options
reasoning.description: Use when the history rows do not expose product names or configurations and each order must be opened; stop once the matching item is found.
reasoning.content: Open each year-matching row with its “View Order” link in a fixed sequence, record which rows were checked, and return to the expanded history after each mismatch to avoid revisiting orders. On the matching order page, read the configuration shown beneath or beside the item name—do not infer size from price, quantity, or the product title—and provide the answer before continuing navigation.

reasoning.title: Require visible item-option evidence
reasoning.description: Use when answering about an item configuration such as Color; do not apply when the question only asks for order-level information already displayed in the history table.
reasoning.content: On the order page, locate “Items Ordered” and verify that the requested item name and its labeled option appear together in the visible page content, scrolling if needed. Do not report a value inferred from narration, another product’s options, or an unobserved section.

reasoning.title: Navigate the full order history
reasoning.description: Use when the target purchase is absent from the account dashboard’s recent orders; not when it is already listed there.
reasoning.content: From “My Account,” open “My Orders,” then use the pagination controls to move through the reverse-chronological order list. Open candidate orders via their visible order-detail link and return to the same history page if the item is not present.

reasoning.title: Verify configuration in the line item
reasoning.description: Use when an order-detail page is open and the task asks for an item option such as color, size, or configuration; do not answer from the order date, order number, or an assumed product match.
reasoning.content: Scroll or otherwise inspect the order page until the product line and its labeled option rows are visibly rendered. Report only the value shown beside the requested label, and withhold the answer if the captured page content ends before those details appear.
